notes.title: Astor: Blade of the Monolith Patch 3!
notes.content:
Hello Warriors of Gliese!

We're excited to bring you another update for Astor: Blade of the Monolith! This patch includes a variety of improvements based on your feedback and our ongoing efforts to enhance gameplay and balance.

Gameplay Adjustments


 Weapon Balance: Balanced various weapons, with special attention to the Gauntlets and Hammer. Adjustments aim to improve effectiveness and ensure each weapon feels distinct and powerful.
 Construct Companions Enhancement: Adjusted Construct Companions to hit harder and exhibit more aggressive behavior in combat.
 Boss Balance Rework: Several bosses have been reworked to provide a more challenging experience, aligning their difficulty better with regular enemies.
 Improved Block Responsiveness: The responsiveness of the block action has been enhanced, making parries more accurate and timing-dependent.
 Boss Attack Fixes: Fixed issues where some boss attacks could be interrupted unexpectedly, causing behavioral inconsistencies.
 Block Drop Construct Adjustments: Increased cooldown and adjusted damage values for the Block Drop construct. Now rewards skilled players with a 1.5x damage multiplier when used with a combo of 10 or higher.
 Aerial Combat Adjustments: Melee enemies will no longer throw projectiles while the player is performing aerial attacks, eliminating unfair interruptions.


New Content

 New Crystal Life Items: Added new crystal life items to the store:

[olist]
 Healing Crystal
 Health Crystal Boost Lv 1, Lv 2, and Lv 3
[/olist]

 New Awakening Tutorial: Added a reinforced tutorial for the Awakening mechanic to provide clearer guidance and understanding for players.


Audio and Visual Enhancements
Combat Music Intensity: Adjusted the intensity of combat music to change more gradually based on the number of hits performed in combat, providing a smoother and more natural transition.
Golem King Boss Audio: Improved audio for the Golem King boss encounter for a more immersive experience.
Collision Improvements: Enhanced tree collision mechanics to improve realism and gameplay interactions.

Bug Fixes and Improvements

 Challenge and Replay Fixes: Addressed various bugs related to challenges and replay functionality.
 Renamed map tab in adventure menu to collectables to better reflect the purpose of this section
 

We're committed to delivering the best experience possible in Astor: Blade of the Monolith. 

Your feedback continues to be invaluable to us, so please keep sharing your thoughts and experiences!

Thank you for your support and dedication to exploring the world of Gliese with us.

— The C2 Game Studio Team

notes.title: Astor: Blade of the Monolith Patch 1.1.0 is out!
notes.content:
Greetings, Warriors of Gliese!

We are excited to bring you the second update for Astor: Blade of the Monolith! Your feedback has been instrumental in helping us identify and fix issues, as well as improve the game. We hope you continue to share your thoughts with us as you explore the mysteries and dangers of Gliese.

Update 1.1.0 Patch Notes:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/228be910c3af6b1a2e860f07e1c573bd69a68c0a.png
Community Feedback Implementation

 Hammer Rune Ability: Adjusted the hammer's rune ability to be more effective and responsive, ensuring it hits enemies more reliably and faces their direction when activated.
 Additional Controller Mapping Presets: Added 2 extra presets based on feedback.
 Improved Drowning Mechanics: Falling into deep water no longer deals damage to the player, improving the drowning mechanic for a more seamless gameplay experience.
 Enhanced Climbing Sequences: Improved climbing sequences, particularly in the Start Camp level, to provide smoother and more intuitive traversal mechanics.

Bug Fixes

 Cinematic Loops: Fixed an issue where the final cinematic sequence from Kalios to Lyceum could get stuck in an indefinite loop.
 Respawn Glitches: Resolved a rare bug where falling into water would cause the player to respawn on top of the water instead of on solid ground.
 Character Behavior: Corrected an issue where Zan would walk out of cinematic scenes in Start Camp. Zan will now stay in place as intended. (He's not that shy anymore). 
 Low Health Warning: Improved the low health status effect to alert players earlier, giving more time to react and heal.
 Collectable Items: Fixed the collectable item counting in levels, which previously showed incorrect totals on the map.
 Chapter Replay Fix: Addressed an issue in the replay chapter of "Inside the Monolith" during the fight against Haken, ensuring the encounter progresses smoothly.
Fixed the bug with the achievement: Ultimate Life Form not triggering properly at all times. (Players that already bought all the upgrades can unlock it by opening a store and waiting for a few seconds)

We are continuously working on implementing your suggestions and addressing other reported bugs. Your support and feedback are invaluable to us, and we encourage you to keep sharing your experiences as you journey through Gliese. If you can, please leave us a review - it really helps let others know about the game! 

You can leave a review here

From all of us at C2 Game Studio and TinyBuild, thank you for your continued support. We look forward to seeing you wield the Blade of the Monolith with newfound power and precision!

— The C2 Game Studio Team

notes.title: Devlog #3: The Art of Astor
notes.content:
Exploring the Art of Astor: Blade of the Monolith

Welcome to our deep dive into the artistry behind Astor: Blade of the Monolith. In this blog, we'll delve into the evolution of the game's art style, the process behind developing characters like Astor, and the challenges and breakthroughs encountered along the way.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/a598de7126e6e0cdd3098f534aa86d01ad40401e.png

Evolution of the Art Style

The art style of Astor: Blade of the Monolith underwent significant evolution throughout its development journey. Starting with a flat toon style, the team eventually transitioned to a stylized modern rendering approach. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/7a99b48844b3a7f1793290014d25b162e3ec05af.png

Early inspirations from games like Zelda Breath of the Wild set the tone, guiding the team towards a balance between shapes and color palette reminiscent of that beloved title. However, it was decided that the team wanted to avoid a cell shaded look, and later took influence from Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart. That game inspired a shift towards adding more detail and realism while maintaining a cartoon-like visual identity resulting in the game’s captivating blend of modern rendering techniques and saturated toon-like textures that immerse players in a visually stunning world.

Balancing Realism and Fantasy

Achieving a harmonious balance between realism and fantasy was crucial in crafting an immersive world for players to explore. By employing modern realistic rendering techniques, the team added depth and dimension to materials, enhancing the game's visual fidelity without compromising its stylized aesthetic. Careful tuning of parameters ensured that the game retained its unique style while offering high-definition details akin to modern gaming experiences.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/ef7f0d24c178e68489379a1373a54f63719c002d.jpg

Developing Astor's Character Design

Astor, the enigmatic protagonist of Astor: Blade of the Monolith, underwent an extensive process of development to ensure he felt both unique and integral to the game world. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/7531b4e08beee6efd3b8089a4a60aa368edd0ee5.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/c963a994c7ee8d7cd4d0ea30bfe0b9976f5e9830.png

Iterations were plentiful as the team sought to create an iconic character with whom players could relate. Ultimately, Astor emerged as a Diokek - a reflection of bravery and fragility in a genre dominated by strong heroes. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/612cc6b14f34a0c1654177d664bfd8645b3d9429.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/52be9ad8d55573b33708a925c3fd0d8be85f3060.png

His design speaks to the essence of humanity, embodying the potential for greatness and the pursuit of dreams.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/dfca50e08b7ccf8565d6967391247aae6ddb9ce7.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/526ca9bbb91c66cf9605e311307f7ab054b6e431.png

Character design in Astor: Blade of the Monolith was guided by a desire to ensure each character served a purpose within the narrative. The Diokek were  initially conceived as adversaries, but killing them felt really bad, so they evolved into a whimsical and magical race worthy of protection - and the race of the player character.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/aadc30cec0a339d0d9e6ec841e193d56e0067afa.png

Conversely, the Hiltsik emerged as twisted versions of the Diokek, their creepy demeanor adding depth to the game's universe. The decision to integrate masks into the characters' bodies further enriched their identities, linking soul to form in a literal and symbolic manner.

Challenges and Breakthroughs

The journey of creating Astor: Blade of the Monolith was not without its challenges. However, two significant decisions shaped the game's art style: making Astor a Diokek and incorporating realistic properties into materials. These choices, though daunting, ultimately propelled the game towards its final iteration!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/4eab1610573574e63828089cdb557326ad6510da.png

That’s all for our art devlog, keep an eye on all of our social channels to keep up with the latest information on Astor: Blade of the Monolith!

X (formerly Twitter)
Instagram
Facebook

notes.title: Devlog #2: Exploring the Mystical World of Gliese
notes.content:
Welcome to our deep dive into the captivating world of Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients. In this devlog, we’ll explore the world of Gliese, introduce our hero, Astor, and some of the peoples who you’ll meet on your adventure! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/425f6e40da8f0142abb7435a7deb22953e39a070.png

Gliese: A World Shrouded in Mystery

At the heart of our game lies Gliese, a mystical world where a towering Monolith stands as a silent sentinel. The origins of this Monolith are shrouded in mystery, its purpose unknown to the inhabitants of Gliese. Throughout the ages, civilizations have risen and fallen, each leaving their mark on the landscape and shaping the course of history.

Buried beneath the sands of time, ancient ruins dot the landscape of Gliese, serving as a testament to the greatness of past civilizations. Some worship the Monolith as a deity, while others have dedicated themselves to unlocking its secrets. These ruins hold the key to unravelling the mysteries of Gliese and uncovering the truth behind its ancient past.

Exploring the Three Regions of Gliese

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/767cd831a80a7a199e8519fe2aef45e57f904d1d.png

In our journey through Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients, we'll explore three distinct regions of Gliese:

Proxima Grasslands: A lush forest teeming with vibrant foliage, bathed in the hues of red and purple. Here, nature reigns supreme, and hidden secrets lie waiting to be unearthed amidst the dense vegetation.

Kalios Mountains: Towering peaks cloaked in snow dominate the landscape of the Kalios Mountains. Here, adventurers brave the treacherous terrain in search of ancient relics and the wisdom of the ancients.

Xanios Desert: A vast expanse of sand stretches endlessly across the Xanios Desert, where the capital city of the makers once stood. Here, the Monolith stands tall and unchanged, a silent witness to the passage of time.

Fun Fact:

Did you know that Gliese is named after an actual star system located 20 light-years away from Earth? While our Gliese doesn't represent any specific planet within this star system, it's intriguing to think about the possibility of discovering a world with red trees and a mystical Monolith.

Meet Astor: The Brave Protagonist

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/8d8fc7a19897b170e6883db30b805d231e701fd2.png
“A Hero will rise from the most unlikely of places. A Hero will face evil. A Hero will emerge triumphant. A Hero will transform Gliese...”
— fragment from History of the Monoliths IV
Astor, a youthful Diokek, spent his days exploring the dense woods alongside his steadfast companion, Zan. While Zan's curiosity often led the way, it was Astor's unwavering bravery that propelled them forward into the depths of ancient ruins. Their adventures took an unexpected turn when Astor was bestowed with a remarkable gift: the ability to harness the boundless energy of the Monolith.

Empowered by this newfound ability, Astor embraced his role as a protector and liberator of the oppressed Diokek. With courage as his guiding force, he embarked on a daring journey to confront the Hiltsik menace and safeguard his people and friends. Astor emerged as a beacon of hope amidst the darkness, venturing into uncharted territories to secure a brighter future for all Diokek.

Unveiling the Diokek: 

The Diokek, a gentle and peace-loving race, find solace in the hidden sanctuary of Crystal Haven, their subterranean city. While their existence echoes the ways of the enigmatic makers, much of their knowledge about this ancient civilization remains veiled in mystery and legend. Central to their beliefs is the Diokek mask, serving as a conduit between soul and body, guiding them in their journey towards the Monolith's source upon passing.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/228be910c3af6b1a2e860f07e1c573bd69a68c0a.png

Encountering the Hiltsik: 

In stark contrast to the Diokek's tranquility, the Hiltsik stand as formidable warriors, imposing their dominance and oppression upon the Diokek. With a culture steeped in combat and devoid of remorse, they force many Diokek into hiding underground. Recent surges in Hiltsik activity, fueled by Astor's awakening powers, have intensified their aggression and expanded their militaristic pursuits.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/21700ac6dadd7500d70d8378261313fe8975205e.png

Delving into Ancient Legends: The Mysterious Makers

Among the shadows of history loom the mysterious makers, a civilization long vanished yet shrouded in myth and legend. Believed to be the architects of the Diokek and creators of the enigmatic structures scattered across the world, they wielded powers that bordered on magic, powered by their connection to the Monolith. Astor's quest to uncover the truth of their legacy holds the key to saving the future from the shadows of the past.

Before we sign off, we have an exciting announcement to share! We're currently in the process of rebranding Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients. Stay tuned for more news and updates in the near future!

That's all for now! Thanks for tuning in to this Devlog update on Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients. Until next time, keep honing your combat skills and prepare for the adventure of a lifetime!

notes.title: Devlog #1: A look at the Monolith: RotA Combat System
notes.content:
Welcome to an exciting update on Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients development! Today, we're diving deep into the heart of the game - its combat system 

Drawing Inspiration from Legends

Inspired by beloved classics like Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, Nier Automata, and God of War, we've crafted a combat experience that's both thrilling and accessible - we want players to feel like true powerhouses, effortlessly dispatching foes with a blend of skill and style. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/200584e3ffe03e84cdd04741b84564ca6ed2e8d4.png

We've crafted the combat experience to be intuitive, allowing players to feel fully immersed in the character of Astor. Our focus on maintaining momentum ensures that each encounter feels visceral and dynamic, enhancing the overall satisfaction of engaging in combat within the game. After mastering the fundamentals, combat in Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients flows seamlessly. 

Accessibility with Depth

One of our primary goals with Monolith's combat system was to make it accessible to newcomers while still offering depth for seasoned gamers. We've achieved this by designing combat to make it easy to keep combos going, swiftly changing from target to target, where you are provided with plenty of offensive and defensive options. Whether you're a newcomer to the genre or a veteran, we think there's something for everyone to enjoy.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/b869a700688c5fbde77d2b73c639ed755dbac653.png

For those of you who want to really explore the combat system, you’ll find you have an awful lot of options to choose from when dispatching your enemy. Different enemies will have different weaknesses - for example, you can use blunt weapons to destroy an enemy's shield or a strong air attack to knock a flying enemy to the ground. If you successfully combine moves together into a combo, you will get the opportunity to perform a Runic Finisher, a powerful attack which will change depending on your equipped weapon.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/0a9a04c302ce42ad63b0c7ee6fa09823f92fc12a.png

Runic constructs provide an extra layer of personalization and strategy, these are abilities that you equip and enter a cooldown when used. You can summon companions, decoys, shields and even powerful AOE attacks!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/5bfaa60f06ffa7b6a1062313c80749726cfdb686.png

Our combat system is all about providing choices for the players and allowing them to experience the fight as they wish. New players will stick to the basics, but experienced players will have the tools to express themselves and dispatch enemies in a deadly and efficient dance of slashes, crushes, blasts and summons. 

Weapons and Abilities

The default weapon - a sword,  is acquired very early on in the tutorial. As the game progresses you’ll collect resources that allow you to unlock skills, including combos and finishers.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/8bcbe31bd06d2cec6f01a90bd6871ed87a96207c.png

Throughout the game, you’ll discover three more types of weapons: a pair of Gauntlets, a Spear, a Hammer and a ranged attack. You’ll also unlock a power summon skill called constructs which will allow you to bring forth tornados, minions, robots and more as you progress through the game. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/66d61702c58f9ee624564aeb597562f141469bfa.png

In combat, the player can simultaneously use weapon attacks, ranged attacks and summoning constructs. Both weapon attacks and ranged attacks will have light, heavy and charged attacks, which, when combined, can form powerful combos. These combos will allow you to activate Runic Finishers.

Epic Boss Battles

Let’s be real here, what would a game like this be without epic boss battles? In Monolith, you will face off against 10 formidable bosses, each with their own distinct abilities and combat styles. These encounters will test your skills like never before, requiring quick reflexes, strategic thinking, and mastery of your chosen weapons and abilities.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44358956/64f23fcb0ad6b9dcae39a4104cd705080bdd48b2.png

Challenges Await

The challenges don't end with boss battles. Players can also tackle a series of special challenges accessed through portals scattered throughout the game world. From facing waves of minions to rematches with bosses, these challenges offer additional opportunities for players to hone their combat prowess and earn valuable rewards. And for those looking for an extra challenge we offer a hard difficulty level and a ‘new game +’ feature.

Before we sign off, we have an exciting announcement to share! We're currently in the process of rebranding Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients. Stay tuned for more news and updates in the near future!

That's all for now! Thanks for tuning in to this Devlog update on Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients. Until next time, keep honing your combat skills and prepare for the adventure of a lifetime!

notes.title: Monolith: RotA - A Realm Unveiled
notes.content:
In the ancient annals of time resides Gliese, a realm draped in mystery, where history lies cloaked in shadows and destiny teeters on uncertainty. Across its vast expanse, diverse lands paint a captivating tapestry. From the scorching desert to the vibrant grasslands, deep forests, and towering mountains, Gliese boasts a spectrum of biomes that enrich its essence. Each environment beckons explorers to unearth their secrets, discover hidden temples, explore caverns, and undoubtedly revel in the manifold wonders that Gliese holds.

BIOME: THE DESERT
[previewyoutube=U9ke9s5SPu8;full][/previewyoutube]
Stretching across a sparse and arid region, the Xanios Desert might have once been the dwelling place of Gliese’s most ancient civilization. Its proximity to the Monolith infuses it with the energy flowing from the monument.

Despite being sparsely populated, nomadic groups of Diokek call this place home. However, danger lurks in the form of frequent Hiltsik activity and the presence of aggressive giant spiders… making this area perilous to explore!

BIOME: THE FOREST
[previewyoutube=LxuXy4OkiGk;full][/previewyoutube]
The Deep Forest, a realm shrouded in an aura of mystery, remains secluded and largely uncharted, veiled by an intricate vertical labyrinth of towering trees and dense foliage. This overgrown region presents a challenging landscape, where navigating the twists and turns tests even the most seasoned explorer.

Legends speak of a hidden grove where the whispers of ancient wisdom echo, guarding its secrets with a natural grandeur that entices explorers while cautioning them against the risks that lie within. Navigating these depths will require much more than courage!

BIOME: THE MOUNTAINS
[previewyoutube=TxRrncsu6GM;full][/previewyoutube]
The snow-capped peaks of the Kalios Mountain Range beckon adventurers, yet their beauty masks the danger within. Harsh temperatures and fierce winds make this region challenging to explore. Hosting a small Diokek village and a unique breed of Hiltsik adapted to the freezing climate, the area faces threats beyond the creatures that inhabit it.

BIOME: THE GRASSLAND
[previewyoutube=cgnBifJaFRo;full][/previewyoutube]
Nestled within the grasslands, the Sacred Lake glistens with serene waters, while the Firefly Forest enchants with a sort of autumnal magic, both thriving within the expansive plains.

Rich with lush vegetation and sprawling forests, the Grasslands provide expansive views that captivate with their natural beauty. Home to Astor and Zan, this area is rumored to serve as the passage to a hidden Diokek City, shrouded in mystery itself.

notes.content:
https://i.ibb.co/mCj4sPj/r54-Vc-LO-1536x864.jpg

Our demo for Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients is live and ready for download until October 16th. We’re so excited to share it with you, and can’t wait to hear what you think!

October 13th Patch Notes:
Features:

 Input Remapping
 Camera Sensitivity Settings
Localization In All Languages:

 Spanish – Latin America
 French
 German
 Japanese
 Korean
 Portuguese – Brazil
 Russian
 Simplified Chinese
 Traditional Chinese
Adjustments:

 General UI/HUD improvements
 Auto dash changes to manual dash with RT or Shift Keyboard
Bug Fixes:

 Players can now interact with a ‘Button’ to open the first ‘Gate’ before killing the enemies.
 ‘Zan’ no longer gets stuck on the stairs when investigating the room with ‘Astor’.
 All inputs will no longer be lost when interacting with the portrait while talking to ‘Zan’ in the ‘Temple of Soma’.
 ‘Purple Crystal’ will now respawn after loading an autosave where the player has already destroyed it at the ‘Temple of Soma’
 ‘Resolution Scale’ is now translated into some languages in the ‘Graphics’ menu.
 ‘Runic Shield’ tutorial can now be completed when reloading an autosave without finishing it at the ‘Temple of Soma’.
 Enemies will now spawn when reloading a save file without killing them in the wing entrance at the ‘Temple of Soma’.
 ‘Astor’ can now talk with ‘Zan’ in the portrait room when going there for the first time at the ‘Temple of Soma’.
 ‘Crystal’ can now be interacted with when reloading an autosave in the end of the ‘Religion Wing’ at the ‘Temple of Soma’.
 ‘Crystal’ can now be interacted with when reloading a manual save file after it is already activated in the ‘Main Chamber’ at the ‘Temple of Soma’.
 ‘Pickup’ is now translated into any language besides ‘English’ when interacting with the ‘Shard Upgrade’.
 ‘Apply’ typo has been fixed in the ‘Graphics’ menu when the game’s language is set to ‘Portuguese’.

notes.title: Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients Joins Steam Next Fest!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=5M9CkuNnD2A;full][/previewyoutube]
Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients is a highly-stylized, action-RPG set within the vibrant, mystical world of Gliese. It will release on PC, PlayStation 4|5, Xbox One, Xbox Series S|X & Nintendo Switch in early 2024.

The fate of Gliese rests on your shoulders, are you ready to become the savior this world needs?

NextFest is here!

We're excited to announce that our demo will be available to the public throughout the entirety of Steam Next Fest, until Oct. 16th!
In the demo, your journey begins as Astor, who is right at the beginning of their epic adventure!

Astor’s search for ancient secrets leads them to the Temple of Soma, a derelict structure ripe for exploration. Will you unearth the answers you seek, or will the path be fraught with peril?

Becoming the savior of the planet is a formidable undertaking, and at this early chapter in Astor’s journey, they have much to learn. A tutorial will introduce you to the fundamentals of combat, setting the stage for the challenges that lie ahead. As you progress deeper into the game, mastering these techniques becomes paramount for survival.

Nevertheless, the journey offers opportunities for growth!

Throughout the demo, you can acquire additional skills and upgrades, gradually enhancing Astor’s capabilities. Most importantly, you’ll unlock a major ability – the Runic Blast. This skill allows you to summon a surge of arcane energy with a multitude of practical uses. Whether as a ranged attack, a means to unseal doors, or even a tool to interact with mechanisms, the Runic Blast will become an invaluable asset in your quest for answers and glory.

An epic tale of good and evil is in the midst of unfolding…

Rise, young hero. The fate of a world awaits.

Notes & Known Issues:


 The demo is only available in English, but the full game will support French, German, Spanish – Spain, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese – Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Spanish – Latin America & Traditional Chinese for interface & subtitles.

 Although the demo is pretty solid overall, we’re still tidying up and fixing bugs. It is a work-in-progress and is not representative of the final product.

 We’re still applying tweaks to balance gameplay, so some elements may feel a bit too easy or too hard at times right now. Let us know how it feels to you!

 Control remapping is planned, but still WIP in this build.

 If you experience issues with your gamepad, please try turning off Steam Input. If you continue to experience trouble, please join us on Discord for additional troubleshooting.


Please Note:

If you need help identifying your PlayStation button mapping from Xbox defaults or setting up your Steam Deck…

We have you covered in our Discord with step by step instructions and infographics!

Join Us On Discord

Wishlist Monolith: Requiem of the Ancients today!
